requirement: Implement OffloadedComputeEngine using loop.run_in_executor with a managed ThreadPoolExecutor, synchronized call_count tracking with asyncio.Lock, and proper exception propagation.
skeleton: Offloaded compute engine offloading blocking sync execution to worker threads without blocking asyncio event loop.
caption: A pure-asyncio compute engine that keeps CPU-bound work off the event loop thread. OffloadedComputeEngine builds one concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor with max_workers defaulting to 4 in its constructor, an asyncio.Lock, and a call_count of zero. run_blocking takes a zero-argument synchronous callable: it increments call_count inside async with the lock so concurrent callers cannot lose an update, fetches the running loop with asyncio.get_running_loop, and awaits loop.run_in_executor with the engine's own executor and the callable, returning the callable's result with its generic type T preserved. Because the executor is created once and reused, four consecutive calls submit four jobs to the same pool rather than spawning a fresh pool each time, and the worker runs on a thread that is not the main thread while the loop stays free to schedule other tasks during the call. compute_hash wraps a nested worker that hashes the input bytes with hashlib.sha256 for the requested number of iterations, defaulting to 50000, and returns the final hex digest of 64 characters, handing that worker to run_blocking. An exception raised inside the worker, such as a KeyError, propagates out of the await unchanged rather than being swallowed into a None result. shutdown delegates to the executor's shutdown with the wait flag so worker threads are released deterministically.

plan.intent: Keep blocking CPU work off the event loop thread
constraints: One thread pool is created in the constructor and reused by every call
The call counter is incremented under an asyncio lock
Work runs through run_in_executor on a worker thread and its result is returned unchanged
An exception inside the worker propagates to the awaiting caller

rationale.teaches: Offloading a blocking call with loop.run_in_executor on a managed ThreadPoolExecutor, a lock-protected counter, and unmodified exception propagation.
rationale.why: Calling the sync function directly or wrapping it in a coroutine returns the correct value while freezing the event loop. The fixture measures loop responsiveness during the call, which is the only way to observe the offload.

ops.docstring: Offload blocking work to a thread pool so the event loop stays responsive.

candidates.why_wrong: The blocking function is called directly on the event loop, so every other task stalls for its full duration.
Wrapping the call in an inner coroutine still runs it on the loop thread, so the loop blocks exactly as before.
A fresh ThreadPoolExecutor is created per call and never shut down, so threads accumulate across calls.
call_count is incremented without the lock, so concurrent calls lose updates.
Exceptions from the worker are swallowed and None is returned, so callers cannot tell failure from a None result.
